name: Smart Solutions
overview: Wireless Push Buttons for Flexible, Infrastructure-Free Industrial Control": Air-Push Series

The Air Push Series Wireless Push Buttons are a revolutionary battery-free wireless control solution that enables push button control signals to be transmitted wirelessly to receivers without any wired connection, wireless infrastructure, or battery power supply — making industrial push button control truly portable, relocatable, and infrastructure-independent. Utilising energy harvesting technology to generate the wireless transmission energy from the mechanical press of the push button itself, the Air Push Series eliminates both the wiring and the battery management challenges of conventional wireless push buttons, delivering the simplest, most deployment-flexible wireless control solution available for industrial automation.

The energy harvesting principle behind the Air Push Series is elegantly simple and operationally transformative. When the operator presses the push button, the mechanical energy of the press is harvested by the button's internal energy converter and used to power the wireless transmission of the control signal in that instant — no battery required, no charging infrastructure needed, no wiring to install. The control signal is received by the paired wireless receiver, which interfaces with the machine or control system through its wired output connection. The result is a wireless push button that can be placed anywhere within range, moved at will, and will never need its battery replaced — because it has none.

The industrial implications of battery-free wireless push button operation are significant. In manufacturing environments, battery-powered wireless devices require a maintenance programme to monitor battery state and replace batteries before they cause device failure — an overhead that increases with every wireless device added to the facility. In safety-critical applications, a flat battery that causes a control device to fail is a serious operational concern. The Air Push Series eliminates both the maintenance overhead and the failure risk of battery dependency, providing a wireless control solution that is available and functional every time the operator needs it.

The Air Push Series is designed for the range of industrial push button applications where wireless deployment delivers genuine operational advantage — including flexible assembly line workstations where the button position must adapt to changing product configurations, ergonomic control positioning that follows the operator rather than being fixed to a machine structure, temporary or reconfigurable production layouts where wired button installation is impractical, and machine guarding applications where a freely positioned acknowledgement button is needed without cable routing through safety guards.

name: Push Button Switches
overview: Specialist Industrial Switches for Circuit Protection, Network Connectivity, and Emergency Stopping
Variants covered: Circuit Breaker Switch · Unmanaged Industrial Network Switch · EBS (Emergency Break Switch)

The Switches category within Esbee's industrial push button switch range covers three specialist switching devices — the Circuit Breaker Switch, the Unmanaged Industrial Network Switch, and the Emergency Break Switch (EBS) — each serving a distinct and critical electrical function in industrial control panels, automation systems, and machine electrical infrastructure.

The Circuit Breaker Switch combines overcurrent protection with a manual switching function in a single panel-mounted device. When a fault condition — short circuit or sustained overload — drives current above the breaker's rated trip threshold, the mechanism trips automatically and interrupts the circuit before thermal damage can occur to conductors, components, or connected equipment. The manual switching function allows the same device to serve as a deliberate isolation point for maintenance operations, providing both protective and operational switching from one compact panel component. The circuit breaker switch is the correct specification for motor branch circuits, control panel supply circuits, and auxiliary equipment supply points where both overcurrent protection and local isolation are required.

The Unmanaged Industrial Network Switch is an Ethernet switching device engineered for direct installation in industrial control panels and automation network infrastructure, providing reliable, deterministic network connectivity between PLCs, HMIs, drives, sensors, and other Ethernet-based industrial automation equipment. Unlike office-grade network switches, the industrial network switch is designed for the electrical noise, temperature extremes, vibration, and DIN rail installation environment of industrial control panels — maintaining network performance and uptime in the electromagnetic and mechanical conditions that consumer-grade switches cannot withstand. The unmanaged configuration requires no software setup, connecting automatically to forward Ethernet frames between ports at wire speed without configuration overhead — the correct choice for fixed-topology industrial networks where plug-and-play connectivity is preferred over managed network features.

name: Limit Switches
overview: Versatile Plastic Body Limit Switches with Multiple Actuator Variants for Industrial Position Detection
Variants: SLPBS3A1 · SLPBS3F5 · SLPBS3B2 · SLPBS3B4 · SLPBS3LP · SLPBS3EE · SLPBS3D · SLPBS3F7

The SLPB Series Plastic Limit Switches are a comprehensive range of industrial electromechanical position detection switches housed in durable, impact-resistant plastic enclosures, available across eight actuator variants to cover the full range of industrial position sensing applications. Each variant in the SLPB series shares the same robust plastic housing and IEC 60947-5-1 compliant contact block architecture, with the actuator head differentiated to suit specific cam geometry, approach direction, and mechanical engagement requirements — from standard roller lever and whisker actuators to push plunger, fork lever, and rotary head configurations.

Plastic housing limit switches are the preferred specification for general industrial position detection applications where the operating environment does not expose the switch to heavy mechanical impact, aggressive chemical attack, or extreme temperatures that would demand a metal housing. The high-impact thermoplastic enclosure of the SLPB series provides excellent resistance to the typical industrial environment — oils, greases, dust, coolant splash, and mechanical contact from cams and machine elements — while offering the cost advantages and corrosion immunity of non-metallic construction in applications where long-term exposure to moisture or mild chemicals would cause metal housings to deteriorate.

The SLPB series actuator variants cover the standard approach geometries of industrial limit switch applications. The A1 and A3 variants feature roller lever actuators for cam-operated position sensing where the actuator must engage a cam or dog approaching from a defined direction. The F5 and F7 variants provide adjustable roller lever configurations that accommodate a wider range of cam heights and approach speeds. The B2 and B4 variants offer fork roller actuators for position sensing of rods and shafts. The LP variant provides a long roller lever for applications requiring the actuator to span a greater cam reach distance. The EE variant offers a coil spring actuator for gentle, continuous contact applications, and the D variant provides a direct push plunger configuration for applications where the target directly depresses the switch actuator.

Standard 24V DC Relay Boards are designed to provide reliable digital input interfacing while ensuring stable performance in industrial environments. Built with robust electronic components and a carefully engineered PCB design, these relay boards deliver dependable switching functionality for automation panels, machinery control systems, and electrical equipment.

The relay board incorporates a freewheeling diode across the relay coil, which protects the circuit from back electromotive force (Back EMF). This feature helps prevent voltage spikes that may occur when the relay coil is switched off, thereby protecting sensitive electronic components and improving the overall reliability of the system.

name: Door/Lid Switches
overview: Reliable Rocker Switch for Interior Light Control in Refrigerators and Deep Freezers

The Rocker Switch for refrigerator and deep freezer applications is a precision-moulded electromechanical switching component designed to control the interior cabin lighting circuit of domestic and commercial refrigeration appliances. Activated by the mechanical pressure of the closing door or lid, this switch cuts power to the interior light when the appliance is closed — preventing unnecessary lamp heat generation inside the cabinet and eliminating the wasted energy of a light left running continuously inside a closed cold storage unit. It is one of the most frequently actuated switches in any household appliance, making its reliability and longevity a critical factor in overall appliance quality.

The role of the refrigerator door switch in appliance performance goes beyond simple light control. In refrigerators and deep freezers where the interior light is based on incandescent or older LED technology, a switch that fails in the closed position — allowing the light to remain on inside a sealed cabinet — generates unwanted heat that the refrigeration system must work harder to overcome. This increases energy consumption, accelerates compressor wear, and in worst cases can affect the temperature integrity of stored food. The rocker switch's reliable circuit interruption on door closure is therefore a meaningful contributor to the appliance's energy efficiency and compressor longevity.

The rocker switch mechanism is engineered for the specific actuation conditions of refrigerator door and lid applications. The door seal exerts a defined pressure on the switch actuator as it closes, and the switch must respond to this pressure with reliable, consistent contact actuation — not too stiff to prevent full door closure, and not so sensitive that vibration or minor pressure causes inadvertent switching. The actuator force and travel are carefully calibrated to the door pressure characteristics of the appliance models for which the switch is specified.

Constructed for the temperature and humidity conditions of refrigeration appliance interiors, the rocker switch materials are selected for dimensional stability at refrigerator operating temperatures, resistance to the moisture and condensation present inside cold appliances, and compatibility with the food-safe environment of refrigerator cabinets. The switch body and actuator maintain their mechanical integrity and switching performance across the thousands of door-open and door-close cycles that a busy household refrigerator accumulates each year.

overview: E12 Screw Lamp Holders for Refrigerator and Deep Freezer Interior Lighting

The Bulb Lamp Holder – E12 is a precision-moulded lamp socket designed for the E12 Edison screw base lamp format, providing a secure, reliable electrical connection point for interior lighting bulbs in refrigerators, deep freezers, and cold storage appliances. As the mounting and electrical interface between the appliance cabinet interior and the replaceable light source, the E12 lamp holder is a fundamental component of the appliance lighting system — its reliability, dimensional precision, and material quality directly determining how well the interior lighting functions across the appliance's service life.

The E12 base format (12mm Edison screw) is a common lamp specification in refrigerator and cold appliance interior lighting, used in both domestic and commercial refrigeration equipment across multiple markets. The lamp holder provides the threaded socket that accepts the E12 lamp base, the spring-loaded or fixed electrical contacts that make reliable connection to the lamp base centre contact and outer thread, and the mounting body that secures the holder to the appliance cabinet interior structure at the designed lamp position.

Material specification is a critical engineering consideration for refrigerator lamp holders. The holder must maintain dimensional stability at the low temperatures of refrigerator and freezer operation — typically ranging from +5°C in the main compartment to -25°C or lower in deep freeze sections — without dimensional shrinkage or embrittlement that could loosen lamp retention or crack the holder body. Simultaneously, the holder must withstand the brief but significant thermal shock when the appliance light activates inside a cold cabinet, cycling between cold ambient and the operating temperature of the lamp base with every door opening cycle across the appliance's service life.

The electrical contacts within the E12 holder maintain reliable connection to the lamp base under the vibration of compressor and fan operation, and resist the contact oxidation that can develop in the humid, occasionally condensing environment of a refrigerator interior. Contact plating and spring retention force are selected to ensure low contact resistance and reliable lamp activation across thousands of door-cycle actuations without contact degradation that could cause intermittent illumination.

The PCBA Display for refrigerator and deep freezer applications is a purpose-designed printed circuit board assembly that provides the electronic intelligence behind the user-facing display panel of modern refrigerators — driving temperature readouts, mode and setting indicators, alert notifications, and the user interface through which consumers interact with their appliance's operating parameters. As the bridge between the appliance's sensor and control systems and the consumer's display interface, the PCBA Display is a core functional module that defines the perceived intelligence, responsiveness, and sophistication of the refrigerator's user experience.

Contemporary refrigerators have evolved significantly beyond simple thermostat-controlled cooling boxes. Today's mid-range and premium refrigerators display real-time cabinet temperatures in multiple zones, allow users to set specific target temperatures for refrigerator and freezer sections independently, indicate active operating modes such as quick chill, vacation mode, and super-freeze, alert users to door-open conditions and temperature excursions, and in connected models communicate with smartphone apps and smart home systems. The PCBA Display is the electronic component that enables all of these intelligent user interface functions, processing sensor data and control system states into the visual and tactile feedback the user sees on the appliance front panel.

The PCBA is designed for the specific electrical, mechanical, and thermal environment of refrigerator appliance integration. Board layout optimises the display driver circuit for the display technology used in the appliance — LED segment, LCD, or OLED depending on the product tier — with the signal processing and power conditioning appropriate for the display technology's operating requirements. The board is protected against the humidity and temperature variation of appliance interior and door environments, with component selection and conformal coating specifications matched to the appliance's operating conditions.

Manufacturing quality is a paramount consideration for appliance PCBA supply, as a display board failure creates a complete user interface failure that makes the refrigerator appear inoperable — a high-impact, high-visibility product quality issue that generates consumer complaints and warranty claims. Esbee's PCBA manufacturing and quality processes are calibrated to the zero-defect expectations of appliance OEM supply, with in-circuit and functional testing protocols that verify every board to specification before shipment.

overview: Panel Mounted Panic Switch for Emergency Vehicle Safety Systems

The Panic Switch – Panel Mounted is a robust, safety-critical electromechanical switch engineered for emergency vehicle applications where a fixed, panel-integrated emergency actuation point is required. Designed for seamless integration into the control panels of ambulances, fire trucks, police vehicles, and other special-purpose emergency automobiles, this switch provides operators and passengers with immediate, reliable access to an emergency alert or safety function directly from the vehicle dashboard or interior panel.

Panel mounting offers a permanent, stable installation that ensures the panic switch is always in a fixed, known location — a critical requirement in genuine emergency situations where fumbling for a portable device is not an option. name: Pit Control Devices
overview: Safety-Critical Elevator Pit Switches for Compliant Lift Shaft Access Control

Pit Switches are safety-critical electromechanical switching devices installed in the elevator pit — the space beneath the lowest landing level of a lift installation — to provide essential safety interlocking and access control functions that protect maintenance technicians working in this confined and high-risk area. Designed in accordance with elevator safety standards and regulations, pit switches are a mandatory component in compliant lift installations and play a direct role in preventing inadvertent elevator movement while personnel are present in the pit.

The elevator pit is one of the most hazardous locations in any lift installation. It is a confined space subject to restricted access, potential moisture accumulation, and the ever-present danger of elevator car movement above. When a maintenance technician enters the pit to inspect the buffer, clean drainage systems, check electrical connections, or service pit-mounted equipment, they must be protected from unexpected elevator travel by a reliable safety interlock system. The pit switch is the primary device that enables this protection — interrupting the safety circuit and preventing normal elevator operation as soon as the pit access door is opened or a pit stop switch is activated.

Pit switches are engineered to the exacting requirements of elevator safety standards including EN 81 (European lift safety standard) and equivalent international regulations, which specify the exact switching logic, contact ratings, and installation requirements for pit safety devices. Compliance with these standards is not optional — it is a legal requirement in most jurisdictions for lifts serving the public or operating in commercial premises, making the specification of correctly certified pit switches essential for any compliant elevator installation.

The switch contacts are designed for reliable operation in the demanding environmental conditions of the elevator pit, including exposure to moisture, dust, temperature variation, and the low-frequency vibration generated by elevator machinery during normal building operation. Long-term switching reliability is essential, as a pit switch failure that prevents normal elevator operation can cause service disruption, while a failure that allows elevator movement with a technician in the pit creates an immediate life-safety risk.

name: Car Top Devices
overview: EN 81-Compliant Car Top Inspection Control Station for Safe Elevator Maintenance

The Car Inspection Unit is a safety-certified elevator control station mounted on the roof of the elevator car, providing maintenance technicians with direct, localised control of the lift during car top inspection, maintenance, and fault diagnosis operations. When a technician accesses the car roof to inspect overhead machinery, guide rails, ropes, or car top equipment, the Car Inspection Unit gives them full, safe control of elevator movement from their working position — independent of floor calls, landing controls, and the elevator's automatic control system.

Working on top of an elevator car is one of the most hazardous activities in lift maintenance. The technician is positioned on a moving platform in an enclosed shaft, surrounded by structural steelwork, counterweights, guide rails, and overhead machinery. In this environment, the ability to control elevator movement locally and to stop the car immediately in any situation is an absolute safety prerequisite. The Car Inspection Unit provides exactly this capability, enabling the technician to move the car up or down at regulated inspection speed and to halt movement instantly whenever required.

The Car Inspection Unit is designed to meet the mandatory requirements of EN 81-20 and EN 81-50 — the European lift safety standards that govern inspection control devices — as well as equivalent international elevator safety regulations. Key mandated features include up and down directional controls for car movement at regulated inspection speed, a hold-to-run operating principle that returns the car to the stopped state the moment the directional button is released, and an emergency stop device that immediately interrupts the safety circuit regardless of any other command.

The hold-to-run operating principle is a fundamental safety feature of car top inspection control. Unlike standard push buttons that latch in the activated state, hold-to-run controls require the operator to maintain continuous button pressure throughout any movement of the elevator car. The instant the technician releases the button — whether intentionally, because of a slip, loss of balance, or unexpected event — the elevator stops. This automatic stop-on-release behaviour is the primary protection against inadvertent car movement while a technician is working on the car roof.

name: Auxiliary Controls - Pendants
overview: Heavy-Duty Cam Switches for Crane Electrical Circuit Switching

Cam Switches are robust, multi-position rotary electrical switching devices used in crane applications to control and route electrical circuits associated with hoisting systems, trolley travel, bridge movement, auxiliary equipment, lighting, and maintenance functions. The cam switch mechanism provides positive, multi-position switching with reliable contact actuation at each selected position, making it an ideal solution for crane environments where dependable circuit selection is required under continuous vibration, mechanical stress, and demanding operating conditions.

The rotary cam switch operates through cam-actuated contact blocks, where a rotating cam mechanism mechanically opens and closes electrical contacts in a predetermined sequence as the switch moves between positions. This positive mechanical action ensures precise switching performance and reliable contact engagement at every position. Unlike conventional switching methods, the cam mechanism firmly holds contacts in their selected state, preventing unintended switching, contact chatter, or intermittent connections caused by crane vibration and dynamic load movement.

In crane applications, cam switches are commonly used for motor control functions, direction selection (forward/reverse), speed control circuits, power isolation, maintenance mode selection, lighting control, and auxiliary equipment operation. Their multi-position design enables multiple operating modes and circuit configurations to be controlled from a single compact device, reducing panel complexity and simplifying operator control stations.

Cam switches designed for crane installations are engineered to withstand the harsh conditions found in industrial facilities, ports, steel plants, warehouses, manufacturing plants, and material handling environments. They offer excellent resistance to vibration, dust, moisture, temperature variations, and repetitive switching operations. High-quality contact blocks are rated for long service life, ensuring consistent electrical performance and reliable operation throughout the crane's operational lifespan.
